business_model.claim: PayPal runs a two-sided payments network that connects consumers and merchants. It reported 439 million active accounts across approximately 200 markets at December 31, 2025.
quotes: We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects consumers and merchants with 439 million active accounts across approximately 200 markets as of December 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: Consumers get digital wallets (PayPal and Venmo), money transfers and credit products such as buy now, pay later. Merchants, from large enterprises to small and medium businesses, get branded checkout, unbranded payment processing, buy now pay later, in-person point of sale, business financing, payouts and risk tools.
quotes: We provide large enterprises and small and medium businesses with online branded checkout solutions, including PayPal and Venmo; online unbranded payments processing; PayPal buy now, pay later (“BNPL”) solutions; in-person point of sale solutions; business financing; payouts capabilities; and risk tools.

business_model.claim: The core way it makes money is fees for completing payment transactions, which scale with the volume processed. It also charges for currency conversion, instant transfers and cryptocurrency purchases and sales, but generally does not charge customers to fund or draw from their accounts.
quotes: We earn revenues primarily by charging fees for completing payment transactions for our customers and other payment-related services, which are typically based on the volume of activity processed on our payments platform.

business_model.claim: Revenue falls into two categories: transaction revenues and revenues from other value added services. In 2025 transaction revenues grew $956 million, or 3%, and other value added services grew $419 million, or 14%.
quotes: Our revenues are classified into the following two categories:

business_model.claim: Other value added services draw on credit and partner income. In 2025 they rose by approximately $350 million of interest and fee revenue on loans receivable and approximately $160 million from a partner financial institution, which pays a revenue share on the U.S. credit products. That revenue share depends on the program meeting a minimum return threshold.
quotes: Revenue from the partner institution is earned primarily through a revenue share arrangement based on the economic performance of the program related to our U.S. revolving consumer credit product and PayPal and Venmo branded credit cards, when such performance exceeds a minimum return threshold.

business_model.claim: Interest earned on assets underlying customer balances is part of other value added services, and it fell in 2025 as interest rates declined. This ties part of revenue to interest rates.
quotes: interest earned on certain assets underlying customer account balances resulting from lower interest rates

business_model.claim: Transaction revenue growth is typically correlated with total payment volume (TPV) and payment transaction count. TPV was $1.79 trillion in 2025, up 7%. Third-quarter 2026 net revenue growth was driven primarily by 6% TPV growth.
quotes: transaction revenue growth is typically correlated with TPV growth and the number of payment transactions completed on our payments platform
The increase in net revenues was driven primarily by growth in total payment volume

business_model.claim: Recent revenue is growing modestly. Net revenues were 8,584 in the third quarter of 2026 against 8,417 a year earlier, up 2%. For nine months they were 25,619 against 24,496, up 5% (table in millions).

Transaction expense is the largest cost. It is mainly the cost of accepting a customer's funding source. It was 4,248 of 7,182 total operating expenses in the third quarter of 2026, and 12,798 for nine months against 11,735 a year earlier (table in millions).
quotes: Transaction expense is primarily composed of the costs we incur to accept a customer

business_model.claim: The funding mix drives the transaction expense rate. A card-funded payment costs more than one funded from a bank or an internal balance. Product, merchant and regional mix also matter. The 2025 rate was 0.89% against 0.93% in 2024, helped by a lower share of Braintree volume.
quotes: The cost of funding a transaction with a credit or debit card is generally higher than the cost of funding a transaction from a bank or through internal sources such as a PayPal or Venmo account balance or our consumer credit products.

business_model.claim: Fraud and credit costs sit in transaction and credit losses. These cover customer protection programs, fraud and chargebacks, plus expected losses on consumer and merchant loans. They were 386 in the third quarter of 2026 against 483 a year earlier, and 1,161 for nine months against 1,330 (table in millions).
quotes: Transaction losses include the expense associated with our customer protection programs, fraud, and chargebacks.

business_model.claim: PayPal also earns from lending and sells part of its loans. Loans and interest receivable held for sale were 3,687 at September 30, 2026 against 1,726 at December 31, 2025 (table in millions). The 10-K says it has forward flow arrangements with third-party investors to sell certain loans receivable portfolios.
quotes: We have entered into forward flow arrangements with third-party investors to sell certain loans receivable portfolios.

business_model.claim: Restructuring is an active cost item. Restructuring and other expense was 255 in the third quarter of 2026 against 69 a year earlier (table in millions). A strategic reorganization announced in April 2026 targets at least $1.5 billion in gross annualized run-rate savings over two to three years.
quotes: resulting in restructuring charges of $152 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026

business_model.claim: Revenue is international and exposed to currency. About 42% of net revenues in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 came from customers outside the U.S. Foreign exchange movements and hedging affect both revenues and expenses.
